forcedChoices.reason: «estás solo» reads as loneliness in Spanish; the next clause («no hay otro fuera de ti») shows the sense is uniqueness.
The mandate goes to all will creatures; Spanish forces a number and the context is plural. Same in 1:0.6.
Spanish «realizar» means to carry out; the context is human experience of God, so the sense of becoming aware of him as real fits best.
The quoted words speak to one person.
The participles agree with «una persona», the grammatical antecedent.
English «himself» refers to «personality»; the reflexive avoids a gender choice that English does not make.
English «by faith accept» can be an imperative or a second verb after «should»; the infinitive after «deberían» keeps the parallel reading and does not add a command form that Spanish would force.

forcedChoices.choice: se puede llegar a captar a Dios como realidad
forcedChoices.reason: English 'realized' (grasp as real); Spanish 'realizar' is a false friend, so the sense of perceiving God as real is used.
Keeps open whether 'which is exhibited' refers to the totality or to the divine will, as in the English.
Spanish agreement forces a form; plural covers both the mind and the personality, as the English does.
